If they have a smart TV, the USB plugs directly in and plays with a single button press. For grandparents who live far away, mail the USB in a decorated package with a handwritten note.

The most common obstacle in sharing wedding videos overseas is file size. Here are practical solutions:
Tools like HandBrake (free) can reduce your video file size by 50-70% with minimal quality loss. Export at 1080p instead of 4K for sharing copies — the difference is negligible on most screens.
True accessibility means considering every family member's situation, not just the tech-savvy ones.

Upload your video to Google Drive, Dropbox, or Vimeo and share the link via email or WhatsApp. For family members with slow internet, compress the video to 720p using HandBrake before uploading. You can also split the video into smaller chapters so they can download one section at a time.
Vimeo and some cloud storage platforms offer password protection. Use a simple password that family members can remember (your wedding date works well) and share it separately from the link.

WhatsApp compresses videos heavily, which degrades quality. Instead, upload your video to Google Drive or YouTube (unlisted) and share the link in WhatsApp. Your family gets full quality playback without downloading, and you avoid the compression issue entirely.
When sharing your wedding video internationally, privacy matters.

works well for budget-conscious couples. Set your video to "Unlisted" — only people with the direct link can find it. It's free, works on virtually every device, and most people already know how to use it. The downside: occasional ads and more aggressive video compression.
